name: West International, runway 36R/18L
summary: The eastern of the test field's two parallel airliner runways, 1,310 m east of 36L. Landed on southward (18L) from its northern threshold, the arrivals' runway for traffic from the north and east while 36L departs northward; every end takes a 10 NM final.

sources.length_m: As Cape International's: the 747-400 at its maximum weight on a hot day, Boeing D6-58326-1 rev F 3.3.4, rounded up to 3,500 m.
sources.width_m: FAA AC 150/5300-13B change 1, table G-11 (C/D/E-V): 150 ft.
sources.protection: The same table as Cape International's, approach visibility below 3/4 mile; the test field's ground also keeps a 34:1 funnel clear 10 NM off each end (Airfield.pads_for).
sources.place: 1,310 m east of 36L, the least spacing for independent parallel approaches.
sources.pattern: The outer side at each end: landing north on 36R the pattern is to the east, the right; landing south on 18L it is to the east, the left.
sources.in_use: 18L for arrivals from the air base and the north, 36L for departures: parallel runways used one for arrivals and one for departures, as at most airports with a pair.
